To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the strain, strain uneveness, and the waste fore part area of the ECAE process can be generalized as power functions of the ECAF die geometry, the workpiece length, and the workpiece thickness.
the ECAE strain is proportional to the workpiece length, and it depends on the die geometry in a nonlinear way.

the FEM simulations of ECAE deformation of copper workpieces through 2θ-angular dies with different die radii and channel intersection angles can be generalized by using the derived regression power dependences of the ECAE strain on the dimensionless workpiece and die parameters.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of the regression analysis of FEM-based deformation strain and workpiece waste in ECAE process, which can be useful in the optimization and design of ECAE process for different materials and dies.

the development of a new method of ECAE deformation regression analysis, which is a generalization of FFM simulations results, derived by the introduction of Q-Form 2D software to copper workpiece flow simulation through the 2θ angular die with external radius R and internal radius r in channel intersection zone.
the generalization and improvement of the understanding of the ECAE process.

the present work provides a new approach to the generalization of FEA results for ECAE strains, strain unevenness and workpiece waste for a wide range of ECAE die geometries.
the present work provides an effective and useful tool for the design of ECAE dies, which would be able to achieve a desired level of ECAE strain in the workpiece.

the proposed approach is a powerful and effective tool for ECAE deformation analysis, which allows the generalization of the ECAE process parameters and the optimization of the ECAF process parameters for different materials and different ECAE die geometries.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the derived results of regression analysis of ECEA deformation and strain unevenness are in good agreement with published data and can be used to predict deformation and strain uneveness for the ECAE of workpieces with different geometries and lengths.
the proposed regression analysis of FEM simulations of ECAE deformation is an effective method for the prediction of the ECAE deformation and workpiece waste in the process.
the proposed regression analysis is a promising method to improve the understanding of ECAE deformation processes and their influence on workpiece pressure working state.

the proposed approach allows for the prediction of ECAE strain and strain uneveness in the workpiece with the given geometry of the angular die, which is important for the development of ECAE technology.
